# Option reference

<!-- Generated by
cargo run --bin mind-the-build -- --reference docs/options-reference.md
from the command line's own definition; change that and generate again, rather than
this page. A test fails while the two differ. -->

Every option of every verb, as `mind-the-gap <verb> --help` describes it, with its
default and its variable. [Options](configuration.md) says how options become
defaults, and [commands](commands.md) what each verb does with them.

## Every verb

The process options and the seeds, which every verb takes. A session or a ceremony
takes neither on a line: the process options are fixed when the program starts, and
the seeds are asked for (see [the session](interfaces.md#the-interactive-session)).

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Process** | | | |
| `--log-level <FILTER>` |  | `MIND_THE_LOG_LEVEL` | Logging filter, like MIND_THE_LOG_LEVEL (the flag wins). Same grammar as env_logger, e.g. `info` or `mind_the_gap=debug`. Applied when the process starts, so a session keeps the level it started with. Card traffic, which carries pins and key bytes, is never logged above info. |
| `--plumbing` |  | `MIND_THE_PLUMBING` | Plumbing mode for automation: never prompt, report one JSON object per command on stdout, and stop at the first error. |
| `--config <FILE>` |  | `MIND_THE_CONFIG` | Config file to read defaults from, in place of the user's, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mind-the-gap/config.toml (~/.config/mind-the-gap/config.toml by default); `set` alone shows the files read. |
| **Seeds** | | | |
| `-s`, `--seed <SEED>` |  | `MIND_THE_SEED` | Mnemonic seed phrase: the card seed and the key seed, where neither is given apart. Required for any command that derives: a one-shot invocation fails without it rather than stopping on a prompt, and no command ever invents a seed on its own. Use `generate` to mint one, or run without a verb for an interactive session, which asks for the phrase once and keeps it off the command line entirely. |
| `-p`, `--password <PASSWORD>` |  | `MIND_THE_PASSWORD` | Password of the seed phrase; a typo derives other keys, so `check` shows the seed id. |
| `--card-seed[=<PHRASE>]` |  | `MIND_THE_CARD_SEED` | Card seed phrase, which administers cards, apart from the seed (asked for in a session when given without a value). |
| `--card-password <CARD_PASSWORD>` |  | `MIND_THE_CARD_PASSWORD` | Password of the card seed phrase. |
| `--key-seed[=<PHRASE>]` |  | `MIND_THE_KEY_SEED` | Key seed phrase, which derives the identity and its keys, apart from the seed (asked for in a session when given without a value). |
| `--key-password <KEY_PASSWORD>` |  | `MIND_THE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password of the key seed phrase. |

## generate

Mint a new seed phrase and confirm it was written down.

No options of its own.

## list

List the attached cards, their applets and keys; with a seed, whose they are.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Card** | | | |
| `--app <APP>` |  | `MIND_THE_APP` | The applet to act on; both where omitted, each where the card carries it. One of `piv`, `pgp`. |
| **Derivation** | | | |
| `--algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm every key is derived with: P-256 for PIV and Curve25519 for OpenPGP where omitted; p384 is PIV only. One of `p256`, `p384`, `curve25519`, `rsa2048`, `rsa3072`, `rsa4096`. |
| `--legacy` |  | `MIND_THE_LEGACY` | Derive OpenPGP keys and the admin pin under the legacy scheme (mtg0), from one seed, for cards provisioned before 1.0. |
| `-k`, `--subkey <SUBKEY>` |  | `MIND_THE_SUBKEY` | The device or application the keys are bound to: a step of the derivation, no secret, and named in no certificate. |
| `-d`, `--date <YYYY-MM-DD>` |  | `MIND_THE_DATE` | The key generation: a step of the derivation, and the day its keys and certificates were created (the identity date where omitted, or none, created at the epoch). |
| **Keys** | | | |
| `--key <KEY>` |  | `MIND_THE_KEY` | The keys to act on, comma separated (all three where omitted). One of `authentication`, `signature`, `decryption`. |
| `--slot <SLOT>` |  | `MIND_THE_SLOT` | The PIV slot the decryption key goes to instead of 9d: a retired slot from 82 to 95, to keep a previous or another identity's key. |

## check

Show what the seeds derive, and compare a card with it.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i`, `--pin <PIN>` |  | `MIND_THE_PIN` | User pin (a session asks for it where it matters). |
| **Card** | | | |
| `--app <APP>` |  | `MIND_THE_APP` | The applet to act on; both where omitted, each where the card carries it. One of `piv`, `pgp`. |
| `-c`, `--card <CARD>` |  | `MIND_THE_CARD` | Card to address: a PIV serial, an OpenPGP identifier (MMMM:SSSSSSSS) or a reader name, as `list` shows them; the one attached card where omitted. |
| `--policy <POLICY>` |  | `MIND_THE_POLICY` | Pin and touch requirements of the keys, and of PIV management access (relaxed where omitted; see the policies chapter of the book). One of `strict`, `relaxed`, `never-touch`, `always`, `once-always`, `once-cached`, `always-touch`, `cached-touch`, `always-pin`, `once-pin`, `never`. |
| `--fixed-touch` |  | `MIND_THE_FIXED_TOUCH` | Make the OpenPGP touch requirement unchangeable but by replacing the key, where the card offers it (YubiKeys). |
| `--management-algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_MANAGEMENT_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm of the PIV management key `init` installs (auto picks by firmware). One of `auto`, `aes256`, `tdes`. |
| `--kdf <KDF>` |  | `MIND_THE_KDF` | Whether OpenPGP `init` makes the card take hashed pins through its KDF data object (auto: on a Gnuk, which depends on it). One of `auto`, `on`, `off`. |
| `--no-msroots` |  | `MIND_THE_NO_MSROOTS` | Do not store the PIV certificate authorities in the card's msroots object. |
| **Derivation** | | | |
| `--algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm every key is derived with: P-256 for PIV and Curve25519 for OpenPGP where omitted; p384 is PIV only. One of `p256`, `p384`, `curve25519`, `rsa2048`, `rsa3072`, `rsa4096`. |
| `--legacy` |  | `MIND_THE_LEGACY` | Derive OpenPGP keys and the admin pin under the legacy scheme (mtg0), from one seed, for cards provisioned before 1.0. |
| `-k`, `--subkey <SUBKEY>` |  | `MIND_THE_SUBKEY` | The device or application the keys are bound to: a step of the derivation, no secret, and named in no certificate. |
| `-d`, `--date <YYYY-MM-DD>` |  | `MIND_THE_DATE` | The key generation: a step of the derivation, and the day its keys and certificates were created (the identity date where omitted, or none, created at the epoch). |
| **Identity** | | | |
| `-n`, `--name <NAME>` |  | `MIND_THE_NAME` | Common name of the identity, on every certificate and as the cardholder; at most 40 characters where PIV's certificates carry it. |
| `-m`, `--emails <EMAILS>` |  | `MIND_THE_EMAILS` | Email addresses of the identity, comma separated: OpenPGP user ids, PIV alternative names. |
| `--org <ORG>` |  | `MIND_THE_ORG` | Organization (O) of the PIV certificate subjects, at most 64 characters. |
| `--unit <UNIT>` |  | `MIND_THE_UNIT` | Organizational unit (OU) of the PIV certificate subjects, at most 64 characters. |
| `--country <CC>` |  | `MIND_THE_COUNTRY` | ISO country code (C) of the PIV certificate subjects, two uppercase letters such as DE. |
| `--identity-date <YYYY-MM-DD>` |  | `MIND_THE_IDENTITY_DATE` | When the identity was created: the OpenPGP primary key and the PIV root authority, whose fingerprints it is part of, and the generation of keys without a --date (the epoch where omitted). |
| `--validity <PERIOD>` |  | `MIND_THE_VALIDITY` | How long the keys' certificates are valid, counted on the calendar from the day the keys were created: days, weeks, months or years, as 730d, 2w, 6mo or 2y (unlimited where omitted). |
| `--crl-url <URL>` |  | `MIND_THE_CRL_URL` | Where the PIV revocation lists are published, as a URL ending in a list's name with .crl: each list is published beside it, under that name with the root's algorithm added and an issuing authority's tag after it (alice.crl names alice-p256.crl and alice-p256-issuing-9b3e5d17.crl), and every certificate names its issuer's list (none where omitted). |
| `--intermediate` |  | `MIND_THE_INTERMEDIATE` | Insert an intermediate issuing authority between the PIV root and the slot certificates, one per device and generation. |
| **Keys** | | | |
| `--key <KEY>` |  | `MIND_THE_KEY` | The keys to act on, comma separated (all three where omitted). One of `authentication`, `signature`, `decryption`. |
| `--slot <SLOT>` |  | `MIND_THE_SLOT` | The PIV slot the decryption key goes to instead of 9d: a retired slot from 82 to 95, to keep a previous or another identity's key. |

## init

Reset a card and give it what the card seed derives for it.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i`, `--pin <PIN>` |  | `MIND_THE_PIN` | User pin (a session asks for it where it matters). |
| **Card** | | | |
| `--app <APP>` |  | `MIND_THE_APP` | The applet to act on; both where omitted, each where the card carries it. One of `piv`, `pgp`. |
| `-c`, `--card <CARD>` |  | `MIND_THE_CARD` | Card to address: a PIV serial, an OpenPGP identifier (MMMM:SSSSSSSS) or a reader name, as `list` shows them; the one attached card where omitted. |
| `--policy <POLICY>` |  | `MIND_THE_POLICY` | Pin and touch requirements of the keys, and of PIV management access (relaxed where omitted; see the policies chapter of the book). One of `strict`, `relaxed`, `never-touch`, `always`, `once-always`, `once-cached`, `always-touch`, `cached-touch`, `always-pin`, `once-pin`, `never`. |
| `--fixed-touch` |  | `MIND_THE_FIXED_TOUCH` | Make the OpenPGP touch requirement unchangeable but by replacing the key, where the card offers it (YubiKeys). |
| `--management-algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_MANAGEMENT_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm of the PIV management key `init` installs (auto picks by firmware). One of `auto`, `aes256`, `tdes`. |
| `--kdf <KDF>` |  | `MIND_THE_KDF` | Whether OpenPGP `init` makes the card take hashed pins through its KDF data object (auto: on a Gnuk, which depends on it). One of `auto`, `on`, `off`. |
| `--no-msroots` |  | `MIND_THE_NO_MSROOTS` | Do not store the PIV certificate authorities in the card's msroots object. |
| `--lang <LANG>` |  | `MIND_THE_LANG` | Cardholder language preferences (ISO 639-1), most preferred first; where omitted, `init` writes English and `upload` leaves the card's as they are. |
| `--url <URL>` |  | `MIND_THE_URL` | URL where the public certificate can be fetched. |
| `--login <LOGIN>` |  | `MIND_THE_LOGIN` | Login data, conventionally an account or user name. |
| **Derivation** | | | |
| `--algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm every key is derived with: P-256 for PIV and Curve25519 for OpenPGP where omitted; p384 is PIV only. One of `p256`, `p384`, `curve25519`, `rsa2048`, `rsa3072`, `rsa4096`. |
| `--legacy` |  | `MIND_THE_LEGACY` | Derive OpenPGP keys and the admin pin under the legacy scheme (mtg0), from one seed, for cards provisioned before 1.0. |
| **Writing** | | | |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  |  | Write without asking first. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Only show what would be written. |

## pin

Change a card's user pin with the current one, or with `--reset` set a new one with the card seed.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i`, `--pin <PIN>` |  | `MIND_THE_PIN` | The new user pin (a session asks for it twice). |
| `--current-pin <PIN>` |  | `MIND_THE_CURRENT_PIN` | The card's current user pin (a session asks for it). |
| `--reset` |  |  | Set the new pin with the card seed's puk (PIV) or admin pin (OpenPGP) instead of the current one, which also unblocks a blocked pin. |
| **Card** | | | |
| `--app <APP>` |  | `MIND_THE_APP` | The applet to act on; both where omitted, each where the card carries it. One of `piv`, `pgp`. |
| `-c`, `--card <CARD>` |  | `MIND_THE_CARD` | Card to address: a PIV serial, an OpenPGP identifier (MMMM:SSSSSSSS) or a reader name, as `list` shows them; the one attached card where omitted. |
| **Derivation** | | | |
| `--algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm every key is derived with: P-256 for PIV and Curve25519 for OpenPGP where omitted; p384 is PIV only. One of `p256`, `p384`, `curve25519`, `rsa2048`, `rsa3072`, `rsa4096`. |
| `--legacy` |  | `MIND_THE_LEGACY` | Derive OpenPGP keys and the admin pin under the legacy scheme (mtg0), from one seed, for cards provisioned before 1.0. |
| **Writing** | | | |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  |  | Write without asking first. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Only show what would be written. |

## trust

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FILE` |  |  | The certificate to certify. |
| `--level <LEVEL>` | `generic` |  | How well the identity claim was verified. One of `generic`, `persona`, `casual`, `positive`. |

| `--algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm every key is derived with: P-256 for PIV and Curve25519 for OpenPGP where omitted; p384 is PIV only. One of `p256`, `p384`, `curve25519`, `rsa2048`, `rsa3072`, `rsa4096`. |

| `-n`, `--name <NAME>` |  | `MIND_THE_NAME` | Common name of the identity, on every certificate and as the cardholder; at most 40 characters where PIV's certificates carry it. |
| `-m`, `--emails <EMAILS>` |  | `MIND_THE_EMAILS` | Email addresses of the identity, comma separated: OpenPGP user ids, PIV alternative names. |
| `--org <ORG>` |  | `MIND_THE_ORG` | Organization (O) of the PIV certificate subjects, at most 64 characters. |
| `--unit <UNIT>` |  | `MIND_THE_UNIT` | Organizational unit (OU) of the PIV certificate subjects, at most 64 characters. |
| `--country <CC>` |  | `MIND_THE_COUNTRY` | ISO country code (C) of the PIV certificate subjects, two uppercase letters such as DE. |
| `--identity-date <YYYY-MM-DD>` |  | `MIND_THE_IDENTITY_DATE` | When the identity was created: the OpenPGP primary key and the PIV root authority, whose fingerprints it is part of, and the generation of keys without a --date (the epoch where omitted). |
| `--validity <PERIOD>` |  | `MIND_THE_VALIDITY` | How long the keys' certificates are valid, counted on the calendar from the day the keys were created: days, weeks, months or years, as 730d, 2w, 6mo or 2y (unlimited where omitted). |
| `--crl-url <URL>` |  | `MIND_THE_CRL_URL` | Where the PIV revocation lists are published, as a URL ending in a list's name with .crl: each list is published beside it, under that name with the root's algorithm added and an issuing authority's tag after it (alice.crl names alice-p256.crl and alice-p256-issuing-9b3e5d17.crl), and every certificate names its issuer's list (none where omitted). |
| `--intermediate` |  | `MIND_THE_INTERMEDIATE` | Insert an intermediate issuing authority between the PIV root and the slot certificates, one per device and generation. |
| **Writing** | | | |
| `-o`, `--to <PATH>` |  |  | Where the material goes: a file, a directory for several pieces, or `-` for stdout (never for a secret); QR codes on the terminal where omitted. |

## revoke

Revoke a device's keys, a decryption key, or the whole identity.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind <KIND>` |  |  | What the revocation covers: `subkeys` retires this device's keys of this generation, `certificate` the whole identity and every card with it. One of `certificate`, `subkeys`. |
| `--code <CODE>` | `0` |  | Revocation reason: 0 unspecified, 1 superseded, 2 compromised, 3 retired. A lost or stolen card is 2 if the pin may be known, else 3. |
| `--reason <REASON>` | `Unspecified` |  | Human-readable revocation reason. |
| **Card** | | | |
| `--app <APP>` |  | `MIND_THE_APP` | The applet to act on; both where omitted, each where the card carries it. One of `piv`, `pgp`. |
| **Derivation** | | | |
| `--algorithm <ALGORITHM>` |  | `MIND_THE_ALGORITHM` | Algorithm every key is derived with: P-256 for PIV and Curve25519 for OpenPGP where omitted; p384 is PIV only. One of `p256`, `p384`, `curve25519`, `rsa2048`, `rsa3072`, `rsa4096`. |
| `--legacy` |  | `MIND_THE_LEGACY` | Derive OpenPGP keys and the admin pin under the legacy scheme (mtg0), from one seed, for cards provisioned before 1.0. |
| `-k`, `--subkey <SUBKEY>` |  | `MIND_THE_SUBKEY` | The device or application the keys are bound to: a step of the derivation, no secret, and named in no certificate. |
| `-d`, `--date <YYYY-MM-DD>` |  | `MIND_THE_DATE` | The key generation: a step of the derivation, and the day its keys and certificates were created (the identity date where omitted, or none, created at the epoch). |
| **Identity** | | | |
| `-n`, `--name <NAME>` |  | `MIND_THE_NAME` | Common name of the identity, on every certificate and as the cardholder; at most 40 characters where PIV's certificates carry it. |
| `-m`, `--emails <EMAILS>` |  | `MIND_THE_EMAILS` | Email addresses of the identity, comma separated: OpenPGP user ids, PIV alternative names. |
| `--org <ORG>` |  | `MIND_THE_ORG` | Organization (O) of the PIV certificate subjects, at most 64 characters. |
| `--unit <UNIT>` |  | `MIND_THE_UNIT` | Organizational unit (OU) of the PIV certificate subjects, at most 64 characters. |
| `--country <CC>` |  | `MIND_THE_COUNTRY` | ISO country code (C) of the PIV certificate subjects, two uppercase letters such as DE. |
| `--identity-date <YYYY-MM-DD>` |  | `MIND_THE_IDENTITY_DATE` | When the identity was created: the OpenPGP primary key and the PIV root authority, whose fingerprints it is part of, and the generation of keys without a --date (the epoch where omitted). |
| `--validity <PERIOD>` |  | `MIND_THE_VALIDITY` | How long the keys' certificates are valid, counted on the calendar from the day the keys were created: days, weeks, months or years, as 730d, 2w, 6mo or 2y (unlimited where omitted). |
| `--crl-url <URL>` |  | `MIND_THE_CRL_URL` | Where the PIV revocation lists are published, as a URL ending in a list's name with .crl: each list is published beside it, under that name with the root's algorithm added and an issuing authority's tag after it (alice.crl names alice-p256.crl and alice-p256-issuing-9b3e5d17.crl), and every certificate names its issuer's list (none where omitted). |
| `--intermediate` |  | `MIND_THE_INTERMEDIATE` | Insert an intermediate issuing authority between the PIV root and the slot certificates, one per device and generation. |
| **Keys** | | | |
| `--key <KEY>` |  | `MIND_THE_KEY` | The keys to act on, comma separated (all three where omitted). One of `authentication`, `signature`, `decryption`. |
| `--slot <SLOT>` |  | `MIND_THE_SLOT` | The PIV slot the decryption key goes to instead of 9d: a retired slot from 82 to 95, to keep a previous or another identity's key. |
| **Writing** | | | |
| `-o`, `--to <PATH>` |  |  | Where the material goes: a file, a directory for several pieces, or `-` for stdout (never for a secret); QR codes on the terminal where omitted. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Only show what would be written. |

## run

Run a ceremony: a recipe from a ceremony file, after the recipes it depends on.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RECIPE` |  |  | The recipe to run (the file's first where omitted). |
| `--ceremony <FILE>` |  | `MIND_THE_CEREMONY` | The ceremony file (the user's, or the image's, where omitted). |
| `--record <DIR>` |  | `MIND_THE_RECORD` | Keep a transcript of the ceremony, never a secret, in this directory. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Only show the steps, and what the writing ones would write. |
| `--check` |  |  | Check the whole ceremony file and list the recipe's steps, running none: no card is touched and no seed asked for. |

## quit

Leave the session.

A session's verb alone: on the command line it is refused.

No options of its own.

## set

Set session defaults, `name=value`, by the options' long names; alone, show them.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--save` |  |  | Also write the defaults to the user's config file, where they outlast the session; the one way to set them on the command line. |
| `NAME=VALUE` |  |  | The defaults to set. |

```text
The names a default takes, each an option's long name, which is also its config file
key and, upper cased behind MIND_THE_, its variable:
  Card:        app, card, policy, fixed-touch, management-algorithm, kdf, no-msroots, lang,
               url, login
  Derivation:  algorithm, legacy, subkey, date
  Identity:    name, emails, org, unit, country, identity-date, validity, crl-url,
               intermediate
  Keys:        key, slot
  `run`:       ceremony, record
Each takes `piv.` or `pgp.` before it for a default of that applet alone, as in
`set pgp.algorithm=rsa2048`.
```

## unset

Forget defaults in force, each back to the one beneath it: the environment's, a config file's or the built-in one.

| option | default | variable | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--save` |  |  | Also take the defaults out of the user's config file; the one way to forget them on the command line. |
| `NAME` |  |  | The defaults to forget. |

```text
The names a default takes, each an option's long name, which is also its config file
key and, upper cased behind MIND_THE_, its variable:
  Card:        app, card, policy, fixed-touch, management-algorithm, kdf, no-msroots, lang,
               url, login
  Derivation:  algorithm, legacy, subkey, date
  Identity:    name, emails, org, unit, country, identity-date, validity, crl-url,
               intermediate
  Keys:        key, slot
  `run`:       ceremony, record
Each takes `piv.` or `pgp.` before it for a default of that applet alone, as in
`set pgp.algorithm=rsa2048`.
```
